pages.text: A source of flux S raises the antenna temperature by T = S·A_eff/2k. The receiver hears it over the system temperature T_sys - its own noise, the Galaxy's background (strong at low frequency), rain, and the switching noise of every machine nearby. Integrating a band B for a time τ beats the noise down: SNR = T·√(Bτ)/T_sys. A spectral line narrower than the band is diluted; a pulsar's pulse is smeared by dispersion across the band, by 8.3 µs·DM·B/ν³.
$(thing)Set$(): Frequency ν, Bandwidth B, Integration τ.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Receiver gain drift: ±5%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): The dish has no view of the sky.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): A clearer detection is faster; very long integrations are slower.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)System temperature: T_sys = T_rx + T_RFI + T_rain + T_gal(ν)$(br)Source flux at ν: S(ν) = S₁₄₀₀·(ν/1400)^α$(br)Antenna temperature: T = S·A_eff/2k$(br)Line in band: B/2 − |ν − ν_line|$(br)Signal to noise: SNR = T·√(Bτ)/T_sys$(br)Dispersion smearing: Δt = 8.3 µs·DM·B/ν³
